question: Which Mandulog fish gut contents did the 2015 paper explicitly associate with its source taxon labels, and what prevents treating them as fixed species diets or bait advice?

source.citation: De Guzman, C. E., Tampus, A. D., Valdez, S. A. L., Tumang, V. M. C., Moneva, C. S. O., & Canalita, E. E. (2015). Species Composition and Gut Content Analysis of Fishes in Mandulog River System, Iligan City. Advances in Environmental Biology, 9(19) Special, 23-31.
source.access: The publisher issue page lists the article and pages 23-31. Its linked publisher PDF returned HTTP 403 during this review. Full text was reviewed from a ResearchGate public author-content upload by co-author Annielyn Tampus. The uploaded article identifies AENSI as publisher and prints © 2015 AENSI Publisher, all rights reserved. No article-specific republication permission was verified; only short attributed summaries and links are retained.

studyContext.waterbodyAsReported: Mandulog River system, Iligan City, Philippines; study sites are Bayug Island, Barina-ut, Lambaguhon, Bonbonon, and Mandulog.
studyContext.samplingPeriod: The abstract says fish were collected in May-June 2014; the results describe a one-month sampling period. Exact collection dates are not stated.
studyContext.collectionAndGutMethod: Hired fishers used a seine with 2.8 m height, 14 m circumference, and 10 mm mesh. Authors say fish gut/digestive tracts were removed, cut lengthwise, examined with a compound microscope and illustrations as references, then identified and documented. No prey identification key or item quantification method is described in the reviewed methods.
studyContext.catchSummary: The paper reports 114 captured fish across 18 source taxon labels and five sites. This is the catch total, not a stated count of stomachs examined.
studyContext.coordinates: The paper includes a study-area map but no machine-readable station coordinates or datum/CRS were transcribed. No river geometry or points were derived.
studyContext.identityLimits: The paper's source labels are preserved. No independent taxonomic authority or voucher crosswalk was completed for this study, and genus-only labels such as Ambassis sp., Liza sp., Moolgarda sp., and Antennarius sp. cannot support a species-level identity.

dietEvidence.interpretation: Historical gut contents reported from the Mandulog study; not a fixed or range-wide diet.
The fish remains identified only to genus; do not project this observation to a named Moolgarda species.
Historical gut contents reported from this study and river only.
The paper explicitly reports small fish in G. celebius guts; prey identification is not resolved further. Shell fragments are recorded contents and are not assumed to be nutritionally consumed.
Genus-level source identification only; not a named-species diet profile.
Historical gut contents reported from the Mandulog study; not bait advice.
The paper reports genus-level Ambassis; prey information cannot be projected to a resolved species.
The paper gives no diet-sample count for this species.
Sand and detritus are retained as reported gut material, not treated as prey or nutritional food.

The paper directly describes G. celebius among the small fish found in Antennarius guts, but the predator remains genus-only and the paper reports one Antennarius capture, not a stomach-sample denominator.
Historical gut contents reported from this study; no per-species diet sample count is given.

gutContentsReported: Navicula sp. and Gyrosigma acuminatum diatoms
dietEvidence.interpretation: The diatoms are described as numerous in examined gut contents. This local study does not establish the species' complete or universal diet.
Sand and detritus are recorded material and are not classified here as prey.
Historical gut contents reported from this study and river only.

ambiguousOrNonFoodContents.handling: The paper reports these as gut contents but does not establish whether scales/spicules or shell fragments represent intentionally consumed food, incidental ingestion, or prey remains. Do not label them as prey without corroboration.
Recorded material only; the paper does not establish a nutritional prey item for this source label.

interpretation.safeSummary: The paper gives brief species- or genus-associated gut-content observations for several of its Mandulog samples, including fish remains in Antennarius sp. and Glossogobius celebius. The records are historical and local to five Mandulog sites, and stomach sample counts by taxon, prey quantification, and a prey-identification key are not reported in the reviewed methods. Treat each note as a source-reported observation, not a complete natural diet profile.
interpretation.temporalClaimConflict: The abstract and methods describe collection in May-June 2014 over a one-month period, but the diet discussion attributes dry-season versus rainy-season differences to the study without explaining the seasonal sampling design or the supporting sample dates. That seasonal comparison is not extracted as verified temporal evidence.
interpretation.productUseIfRightsAndIdentityAreResolved: A future diet detail could show source-reported gut observations together with waterbody, collection window, method, missing sample denominator, source taxon label, and identity confidence. Do not merge this with other Mandulog surveys, use it to infer present occurrence, or turn it into bait recommendations.
notSupported: A universal, fixed, nationwide diet for any listed fish.
A bait, lure, catchability, or catch-success recommendation.
A claim that lack of a prey item in the paper means the fish never eats it.
Species-level diet claims for source labels identified only to genus.
A resolved species-diet inference from sand, detritus, shells, scales, or spicules without prey interpretation.
A current Mandulog fish inventory, abundance, water safety, legal rule, access right, or river boundary.

qualityAndRights.evidenceLevel: Primary gut-content study as represented by a public co-author-uploaded article copy; publisher issue page confirms article metadata, but the linked publisher PDF returned HTTP 403 during this review.
qualityAndRights.methodsLimits: The paper says stomachs were examined under a compound microscope with illustrations as references, but the reviewed methods do not define a prey-identification key, individual stomach count per taxon, or quantitative diet metric. The total 114 is the fish catch count, not a confirmed gut-sample denominator.
qualityAndRights.temporalAndSpatialScope: Five Mandulog River system sites, May-June 2014 as stated by the abstract; no coordinates or datum/CRS used. A later dry/rainy-season claim is not supported by a clearly described sampling design in the reviewed text.
qualityAndRights.reuseStatus: The author-uploaded text prints © 2015 AENSI Publisher, all rights reserved. No item-specific open license or permission to republish was verified. Keep summaries in this research-only workspace; no article table, figure, image, or raw stomach data is copied.
qualityAndRights.safetyAndDietBoundary: Gut contents are observations in sampled fish from one river and period; they are not bait advice, current fishery guidance, evidence of current local presence, or proof of a fixed species-wide diet.

disposition.reason: The study supports concise historical gut-content notes but does not report per-taxon stomach sample denominators or detailed quantitative diet methods; some stomach material is not clearly prey, the source has genus-only identifications, the seasonal claim is unclear, and article reuse permission was not verified.

nextAction: The 2014 household fishery abstract is reviewed separately in national-mindanao-mandulog-2014-fishery-prey-survey-review-20261031.json and roadmap step 387; its 'preferred prey' phrase is not direct diet evidence. Next, review the 2024 Mandulog fish-fauna source for methods, locality, taxonomic evidence, and rights without treating its title as proof of present-day 2026 occurrence.
